text:
mira: Heads-up — planning a sweep to change default `prefix_cache_ttl` from 30s -> 300s to cut KV churn and tokenization recompute. Want ops + dashboard signoff before we roll. Any immediate red flags?

alex: Big one is memory pressure on the prefix shards. Increasing TTL by 10x will raise resident set and might bump GC/eviction behavior. Need per-shard mem delta estimate. Also could affect p99 for small models.

jess: From the console side I'd like a way to label this as a 'sweep' so the rollout UX can show it differently from targeted flags. Suggest adding optional `rollout_reason`/`rollout_type` metadata in the config API (non-breaking).

tyler: Can we reuse `purpose` tag we already have on configs? Adding fields is fine but it blows up surface area. Backwards compat is key.

sam: Proposal for safe rollout: 1) dry-run in staging for 48h with traffic replay, 2) 1% live traffic cohort hashed by tenant-id for 2 hours, 3) expand to 10% for 6 hours if metrics stable, 4) full sweep. Telemetry thresholds: require >=5000 sampled requests per step and <2% increase in quota_rejects, <5% mem increase per shard, p99 latency delta <10ms.

ops-bot: Created alert policy `prefix-cache-mem-80pct` -> Pager after 10m. Alert ID: ACL-3742.

alex: We also need a console panel that shows per-tenant cache size and the delta versus baseline so SREs can triage. Right now console only shows global mem. Who owns that?

jess: I can take the console work but need API contract. If we add `rollout_type` here's what I propose: optional string enum {"targeted", "sweep", "dry-run"} + `previous_version` and `applied_by` audit fields (all optional). Non-breaking because clients ignore new fields.

mira: Good. One more operational ask: include a `rollback_token` in apply response so automated playbooks can trigger a safe revert. Last time manual rollback was messy because we couldn't identify the exact apply across shards.

tyler: Prefer to avoid another token to maintain simplicity. We already have `config_version`. If we atomically bump to a new version and our controller keeps the previous version for 10m, automated revert is just set config_version back. That keeps API surface small.

sam: Telemetry gating note — don't compute delta metrics until a warm window of 30 mins after cohort starts to avoid transient flapping. Also require at least 5k successful requests sampled before emitting a pass/fail for the step.

alex: Example dry-run apply (ops playbook):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/configs/apply \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"config_key":"prefix_cache_ttl","value":300,"dry_run":true,"meta":{"rollout_type":"dry-run","operator":"mira"}}'
```

jess: Console will show dry-run flag as orange with hover explaining no traffic change.

mira: Ok. Action items: 1) sam will run staging replay and post mem estimates (today EOD), 2) jess will draft minimal API extension PR (opt-in fields only), 3) alex + tyler to prototype per-tenant mem panel (stubbed with aggregated samples), 4) ops to wire alert to the canary step.

ops-bot: Noted. Pager runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/prefix-cache-sweep

sam: I'll also prepare a replay job and a PromQL draft for the deltas: `rate(prefix_cache_evictions[5m]) / rate(prefix_cache_hits[5m])` baseline vs cohort.

alex: sgtm. If staging numbers look safe we can start the 1% cohort tomorrow morning.

mira: Thanks — thanks everyone. Ping me in thread if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
